description:
The award of the Templeton World Charity Foundation (TWCF) grant entitled “Genetic Rescue of the American chestnut” to the ESF College Foundation is fully restricted in purpose to supporting Dr. Powell’s pre-existing and on-going research effort. Following is an excerpt from the actual grant agreement between TWCF and the ESF College Foundation describing the restricted purpose.  

Researchers at SUNY-ESF have developed a blight-tolerant American chestnut tree, using the tools of genetic engineering that can coexist with the deadly chestnut blight pathogen. Using the tools of biotechnology is a unique and innovative approach to rescuing keystone forest species, but their use also presents several challenges that need to be solved. These include developing a pathway through a regulatory process not designed to handle the restoration of a wild species back to the forests; public engagement, education, and participation to help with the restoration; and being the first to restore an ecosystem by returning a socially historic, economic and ecologically important tree. We will be working with the American chestnut (Castanea dentata), whose loss as an ecologically dominant species in eastern U.S. deciduous forests is an iconic example of the devastation wrought by an invasive pathogen on a native keystone forest species.
